title: S3 storage classes and lifecycle policies
hook: S3 storage classes trade cost against retrieval latency — lifecycle rules automate transition from Standard to IA, Glacier, or Deep Archive.

blocks.text: Amazon S3 Standard is default for frequent access. Standard-IA and One Zone-IA reduce cost for infrequent access with retrieval fee. Glacier Instant Retrieval, Flexible Retrieval, and Deep Archive archive tiers with minutes to hours retrieval. Intelligent-Tiering moves objects automatically. Lifecycle configuration transitions or expires by prefix and age.

entries.plainDefinition: Lower storage cost, retrieval fee, 30-day minimum.
entries.example: Monthly reports accessed once a quarter.

entries.plainDefinition: Archive with millisecond retrieval, higher storage cost than Flexible.
entries.example: Medical images rarely accessed but need instant when needed.

entries.plainDefinition: Automated transition or expiration based on age and prefix.
entries.example: logs/ prefix to Glacier at 90 days, expire at 365.

entries.plainDefinition: Auto-moves between frequent and infrequent tiers by access.

blocks.text: Logs and backups accumulate — lifecycle prevents runaway Standard storage bills. Minimum storage duration charges apply when leaving IA or Glacier early. Wrong class causes retrieval latency in production incidents.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: match access pattern to class. Lifecycle by prefix age. Watch minimum billable days and retrieval costs.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Transition to Glacier then need immediate access — retrieval delay. Intelligent-Tiering monitoring fee on small objects. Lifecycle expire rule on wrong prefix deletes production data.

blocks.text: S3 Glacier Instant for archive with instant read vs Flexible for true archive. How to prove it in production: Storage Lens class breakdown, early deletion charge lines in Cost Explorer, restore drill timing.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: AZ loss risk — not for DR copies

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Moving all data to Glacier day one gets rejected — retrieval pain. Strong answer: staged transitions, test restore, noncurrent version rules.

interviewTakeaways: Match storage class to access frequency and retrieval tolerance.
Lifecycle rules filter by prefix — design keys accordingly.
Minimum storage duration penalties on early deletion from IA/Glacier.
60s: Standard hot. IA/Glacier cold with retrieval delay. Lifecycle by prefix age. Test restore.
commonPitfalls: Glacier for data needed daily — weak answer.
Strong answer: Standard or IA for warm; Glacier for true archive with restore runbook.
No noncurrent version lifecycle with versioning on — cost explosion.
Expiring wrong prefix without MFA or policy guard.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Redis TTL evicts hot cache; S3 lifecycle moves cold blobs — different layers of tiering in Node apps.
